8 Conclusion
The following section presents one further conjecture as well as directions for future investigations.
Conjecture 8.1.
With (i) gcd standing for greatest common divisor, (ii) Ls(i),i∈{1,2} defined as in Section 7 and (iii) n​u​m standing for the numerator of a maximally reduced fraction, we have
g​c​d​(n​u​mLs(1),n​u​mLs+1OPEN(2)))>1,s≥1.
Remark 8.2.
The conjecture was tested on several dozen initial values for which it is true. The conjecture has implications of edge values in consecutive reductions of an initial grid.
This conjecture is a simple example of the plethora of patterns and conjectures that loom in the n-grids and their reduction. In fact these reduction patterns of the n-grids lie in a 5-dimensional space. The five dimensions are as follows.
1. 
n is the number of rows in the initial n-grid
2. 
k is the number of row reductions that produce an n−k-grid under study
3. 
The n−k grid is further dimensionalized by
(a) 
rows, r
(b) 
diagonals d
(c) 
edges e.
The five dimensions allow a richness of perspectives. This paper showed that many patterns abound in these n-grids. It is hoped that [10] and this paper will inspire other researchers to delve more deeply into the fascinating patterns that seem to lurk in these n-grids.
